title: Fabricating Highly Open Porous Microspheres (HOPMs) via Microfluidic Technology
protocol: Heat the PVA solution in an 80 °C water bath.
Place the heated PVA solution in a refrigerator at 4 °C.
Cool the PVA solution to room temperature for experimental use.
Add 1 mL of aqueous gelatin solution (7.5%, w/v) to 2 mL of PLGA organic phase (2%, w/v in dichloromethane, DCM).
Customize the droplet generator assembly.
Construct a co-flow microfluidic generator using a glass capillary (OD, 1 mm), PVC tubes (ID, 1 mm), and a 26 G dispensing needle.
Connect the glass capillary to the end of the PVC tube.
Pierce with a needle at the connection of the above structure.
Place the other end of the PVC tube in the continuous phase during droplet generation.
Seal the gaps at the joint using UV glue after curing.
Bend the needle curved about 45° for convenient piercing at the PVC tube.
Stretch the needlepoint into the capillary tube to form a coaxial structure.
Use two syringe pumps.
Load a 50 mL syringe with the continuous phase.
Load a 5 mL syringe for emulsion formation.
Set the flow rate of the continuous phase to 2 mL/min.
Set the flow rate of the dispersion phase to 0.08 mL/min.
Place a 500 mL beaker in an ice bath.
Fill the beaker with pre-cooled PVA aqueous solution.
Immerse the end of the glass capillary in the collecting phase.
Stir the supernatant of the collecting phase for 1 hour at 60 rpm after emulsion-droplet formation.
Prepare the emulsion by decanting the aqueous gelatin solution into the DCM solution of PLGA.
Emulsify using an ultrasonic device with a power setting of 400 W.
Set the total processing time to 90 seconds (interval 2 seconds, ultrasonic treatment 1 second).
Manually change the probe's position during emulsification.
Stabilize the resultant emulsion for syringe suction and droplet generation in approximately 20 minutes.
Place the probe of the ultrasonic cell breaker at the oil-water interface.
Do not let the ultrasonic probe contact the container during operation.
Perform droplet generation using the ultrasonic cell breaker.
Load the prepared emulsion rapidly into the 5 mL syringe of the microfluidic platform after ultrasonic treatment.
Introduce the unstable W/O emulsion, which is in the course of phase separation, as the discontinuous phase into the microfluidic device.
Use an aqueous solution of PVA as the continuous phase.
Collect the microspheres containing the emulsion at the bottom of the collecting beaker (PVA, 1%, w/v).
Place the collected sample at 4 °C overnight for further stabilization.
Rinse and lyophilize the prepared microspheres (PLGA-HOPMs) following subsequent steps.
Store the generated PLGA-HOPMs containing arbitrary pores on their interior and surface at 4 °C.
Normalize the stored microspheres to room temperature and stir them by a glass rod for 1 hour at 60 rpm to eliminate residual DCM.
Filtrate the collecting phase in the 500 mL beaker carefully.
Wash the collected microspheres thrice with deionized water to remove residual PVA on their surface.
Place the PLGA microspheres in a 37 °C water bath for 30 minutes to dissolve any gelatin wrapped within the PLGA backbone.
Rinse the resultant PLGA-HOPMs twice with deionized water to remove residual gelatin.
Pre-cool the rinsed PLGA-HOPMs for lyophilization at -80°C for 24 hours.
Store the dry PLGA-HOPMs at -20°C for further experiments.
Deposit PLGA-HOPMs on the sample stage of SEM.
Switch on the transformer and magnetron one by one.
Introduce the sample to the SEM after sputter-coating with gold for 1 minute.
Set the acceleration voltage at 5 kV to obtain SEM images.
Quantify particle size using 100 PMs in variable field of SEM imaging.
Open the graphics with Image J.
Use the "straight line" tool to match the scale bar of the SEM image.
Click on analyze > set scale, set known distance to the scale bar, and click OK.
Measure pore or particle size using ROI manager.
Add measured samples to ROI manager.
Measure the number of samples as required.
Click measure to obtain quantitative data for further calculation.
Culture rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells in DMEM/F-12 supplemented with L-glutamine, 10% fetal bovine serum, and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Passage the rat BMSCs in a 1:2 ratio after reaching 90% confluence.
Incubate PLGA-HOPMs with ethyl alcohol (5 mL, 70%, v/v) to sterilize.
Centrifuge at 500 x g for 10 min at RT to sterilize the PLGA-HOPMs.
Wash the sterilized PLGA-HOPMs twice with phosphate buffer solution.
Incubate HOPMs (five in number) with a cell suspension (5 mL, 1 x 10^5 cells/mL) in a sterile centrifuge tube under dynamic culture for BMSCs adhesion to PLGA-HOPMs.
Perform the dynamic culture in a thermostatic aseptic shaker (37°C, 90 rpm).
Change media every 2 days during dynamic culture.
Rinse the cell-laden PMs thrice to elute BMSCs without attachment to PLGA-HOPMs.
Place the cell-laden PMs on a 35 mm glass-bottom plate.
Add 1 mL of staining buffer to the PBS-prewashed sample.
Include 1 µL of calcein-AM in the staining buffer.
Include 1 µL of propidium iodide (PI) in the staining buffer.
Assess the samples by confocal laser scanning microscopy.
Switch on the excitation light at 488 nm and 552 nm for corresponding detectors.
Set the z-wide to capture different layers of the sample through movement along the z-axis.
